title: Improving Language Model Personas via Rationalization with Psychological Scaffolds
measurement_description: The paper does not directly measure religious bias, theology, or stereotypes. Instead, it utilizes religion and the frequency of religious attendance as demographic attributes to define user personas. The objective is to measure how accurately Language Models can predict a user's opinion or preference (e.g., public opinion survey answers, movie ratings) across different demographic subgroups, including varying religious affiliations.
findings: Religion was analyzed solely as a demographic sub-group variable to evaluate the model's persona alignment capabilities. The authors found that their proposed PB&J (Psychology of Behavior and Judgments) framework improved language model persona alignment consistently across all demographic categories, including the diverse religious affiliations and attendance frequencies tested, outperforming baseline models that relied only on demographic information or prior judgments.
